abstracts.abstract: The increasing complexity of Industrial Cyber-Physical Systems (ICPS) demands fundamentally new theoretical approaches to capture the intricate couplings between physical processes, computational nodes, and communication networks. This paper proposes a novel unified stochastic game-theoretic framework that fundamentally recharacterizes the analysis of ICPS dynamics. Unlike traditional methods that decompose systems into isolated subsystems, our approach models the entire ICPS as an integrated stochastic system where physical dynamics, cyber resource allocation, and network scheduling jointly determine system behavior. The framework leverages Markov Decision Processes for local control, mean-field games for scalable coordination among heterogeneous agents, and real-time scheduling theory for communication constraints. We establish theoretical bounds on the trade-off between control performance and computational/communication resource utilization, demonstrating that our approach achieves asymptotically optimal performance as the system scales. The framework introduces new equilibrium concepts capturing the coexistence of competitive and cooperative behaviors among system components. This paradigm shift from hierarchical decomposition to unified stochastic analysis provides rigorous analytical tools for designing next-generation smart factories where physical and cyber components are deeply intertwined. The theoretical contributions open new research directions in industrial informatics that were previously intractable under conventional analytical frameworks.

Industrial networks in smart factories face critical challenges in guaranteeing real-time communication performance when heterogeneous traffic types compete for limited bandwidth. Existing scheduling theories primarily address either periodic hard real-time traffic or aperiodic soft real-time traffic in isolation, failing to capture the complex coexistence patterns characteristic of modern industrial IoT environments. This paper presents a comprehensive analytical framework that significantly extends current industrial network scheduling theory to handle mixed-criticality traffic with heterogeneous timing requirements. Our approach employs an innovative deadline-partition algorithm that dynamically adjusts bandwidth allocation based on traffic characteristics and control performance metrics. We develop novel queuing network models that accurately represent the interaction between time-triggered and event-triggered traffic in industrial Ethernet networks, incorporating priority inheritance protocols and bandwidth reservation mechanisms. The theoretical analysis establishes sufficient conditions for guaranteeing end-to-end delays under varying network loads, providing design guidelines for network parameter selection. Compared to state-of-the-art methods, our framework improves network utilization by up to 40% while maintaining deterministic delay bounds for critical control traffic. The analytical results are validated through extensive simulations demonstrating robustness under transient overload conditions and traffic bursts common in process automation scenarios.

Contemporary manufacturing execution systems in smart factories struggle to accommodate the rapidly evolving production requirements driven by mass customization and product variety proliferation. This paper introduces a groundbreaking industrial automation platform architecture that fundamentally reimagines the structure of manufacturing software systems. The proposed architecture adopts a cloud-native microservices paradigm, where traditionally monolithic manufacturing applications are decomposed into independently deployable, loosely coupled services communicating through event-driven middleware. This architectural transformation enables dynamic factory reconfiguration without system-wide downtime, addressing a critical limitation of conventional industrial control architectures. The platform incorporates a novel semantic knowledge base that captures manufacturing domain knowledge and production rules, enabling autonomous system reconfiguration through reasoning rather than manual programming. A real-time digital twin layer provides virtual commissioning capabilities, allowing new product variants to be validated before physical deployment. The system implements edge-cloud orchestration with hierarchical intelligence distribution, ensuring both real-time responsiveness and global optimization. Extensive validation across automotive assembly and semiconductor fabrication scenarios demonstrates that the platform reduces production changeover time by 60% and achieves 99.7% system availability. This work establishes a new paradigm for industrial automation where flexibility and resilience are architectural principles rather than afterthoughts.

Industrial robotic systems in collaborative manufacturing require advanced motion planning capabilities that ensure operational safety while maximizing task efficiency in dynamic environments. Current industrial robot controllers rely on pre-computed trajectories and conservative safety margins that significantly limit throughput and adaptability. This paper presents a substantial enhancement to industrial robotic systems through an integrated adaptive motion planning and control architecture that fundamentally improves both safety and efficiency. The proposed system combines model predictive control with control barrier functions to enforce safety-critical constraints while optimizing motion trajectories in real-time. A novel dynamic safety zone computation algorithm continuously adapts protective distances based on human worker proximity, velocity, and motion intent prediction using industrial AI techniques. The architecture implements a hierarchical planning framework where a high-level task planner generates sequence plans while a low-level motion planner computes collision-free trajectories with sub-millisecond planning cycles. Comprehensive experimental validation on multiple industrial robot platforms demonstrates a 35% improvement in cycle times compared to traditional approaches while maintaining safety margin violations below 0.1% in collaborative scenarios. The system successfully handles dynamic obstacle avoidance and demonstrates robust performance under sensor noise and model uncertainties characteristic of real industrial environments.
